title: What Is Dollar-Cost Averaging? The Calm Way Beginners Spread Out Buying
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Dollar-cost averaging means buying a fixed amount on a schedule instead of all at once. It does not guarantee profit or prevent loss. Sources: Investopedia, Fidelity Learning. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: WHEN TO BUY?
scenes.narration: Prices jump around. So how do people decide when to buy? One common idea is called D C A.

scenes.head: WHAT IS D C A?
scenes.narration: Dollar cost averaging means investing a fixed amount on a fixed schedule, like weekly, whatever the price is.

scenes.head: THE IDEA
scenes.sub: MORE UNITS WHEN CHEAP, FEWER WHEN HIGH
scenes.narration: The same amount buys more units when prices are low, and fewer when prices are high. The average cost smooths out.

scenes.head: WHY PEOPLE LIKE IT
scenes.narration: Many people like it because a routine can reduce emotional choices, like chasing hype or panic selling.

scenes.head: THE LIMITS
scenes.narration: But it has limits. It does not promise profit, prices can keep falling, and fees can add up.

scenes.head: BEFORE YOU START
scenes.narration: Only use money you can afford to lose, learn the fees, and understand the risk. This is education, not advice.
